decisions.reason: As a core rye bread close to the bakery’s traditional range, it likely has steady everyday demand and is worth retaining.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen has external quality recognition and fits the firm’s strong seasonal confectionery business, so it is very likely to stay.
Rye mixed bread with seeds matches current customer preferences for hearty artisanal breads and extends the established bread assortment without much risk.
This dark barley malt rye bread is a more niche variant in an already crowded rye bread segment, so management would be relatively likely to discontinue it to simplify the range.
Marzipan Christmas stollen fits the bakery’s seasonal gift and holiday pastry offer and is a natural complement to the successful raisin stollen.
The ancient grain bread supports the firm’s handcrafted, traditional image and offers some differentiation through heritage grains, making continuation likely.
